Params: The scythe blade hovers at your throat.
The tip of the blade dips just barely, drawing a thin line of red across the side of your neck—
You lie pinned to the cold ground, exhausted by using your power moments before.
Her voice comes out flat and hollow, with no inflection at all.
I've been lying to you this whole time.
The invitation, the ball, the path we took together... All of it was just to lure you here.
You were nothing more than a sacrifice from the very start.
You stare into those crystal-red eyes as empty as the void itself.
After a beat of silence, you let out a quiet laugh.
She's fooled me plenty of times before.
And she was more convincing than you are every time.
The blade presses down another inch, but you do not pull back this time.
And right now, you've made your biggest mistake.
That blade just won't come down.
She has to perform this "sacrifice" herself, doesn't she?
Whatever was possessing her withdraws from Nirvatia's body.
Her hollow, crystal-red eyes slightly tremble as her vacant gaze slowly, painstakingly pulls back into focus.
The Mist behind Nirvatia takes shape, and a low, layered laughter rises from all directions.
Countless gray shadows pull free from the depths of the Mist and converge behind her, stacking and climbing until they solidify into one colossal dark mass.
The silhouette has countless layers, each one faintly human. Generations of ancestors have all fused into one frame.

I don't want to spend the rest of my life carrying the weight of your life...
You watch her, your expression soft.
The forbidden grounds are silent as a grave.
Nirvatia kneels on the ground. Before her, only a handful of ash remains.
The shadow leans in from behind her, his voice carrying a satisfied calmness.
A thread of near-transparent light is drawn slowly from Nirvatia's chest—
The Lone Emperor draws it into himself.
The countless layered silhouettes of the human form swell with it.
Such beautiful pain... A thousand years, and never once have I tasted something so rich.
Then a dark surge flows back through the bridge between.
The thorn-like black markings coiling around Nirvatia crack and splinter, crumbling to dust.
The curse is lifted. From this day forth, the power of the undertaker is yours completely.
Go now, head of the Velosenne family.

And yet she reaches out, her fingers grasping for the handful of remaining ash—
It is no use. The ash slips through her fingers, until nothing remains.
Your voice comes from the darkness beyond the light.
Nirvatia's head snaps up. The moment she sees you, she freezes.
Her cheeks are still wet with tears, yet a smile breaks across Nirvatia's face.
The layered silhouettes lean forward as one.
Ripples of disruption stir between the Lone Emperor's layered outlines.

Inside her M.I.N.D., I saw how she weaved false memories.
She can plant false memories in someone's mind.

You tilt your head toward Nirvatia.

From deep within the mass, faint, fragmented whispers begin to question each other, like a parliament fracturing from within.
Weren't you supposed to be the sacrifice? You're still alive, so how is it complete?
The rite is complete, and I'm still standing. There's only one conclusion.
What it demanded was never death.
What it wanted was an offering of a feeling. A real feeling.
You hold the Lone Emperor's gaze, your eyes slowly turning cold.

Nirvatia freezes for just a moment, then it clicks for her.
Every head of the family cut down the ones they loved most upon this altar.
How would they live on, having destroyed the person they loved most?

"For the family... it was all for the family..."
"I'm sorry... I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry..."
Nirvatia stands frozen, her eyes fixed on the Lone Emperor as he tears himself apart.
You can't ask the future to stay wrong just because you've been wrong.
Every figure freezes at once, then snaps back into alignment in a way that is inhuman—
Rage is the last thing holding this shell together.
The Lone Emperor rises with a thunderous crash. His massive shadow rolls over the light as the countless voices merge back into a single, shrieking roar.
In the name of Velosenne, I command you—
Scythe in hand, she walks, one step at a time, until she stands before you.
But her blade's tip points toward the crumbling Lone Emperor.
Have you forgotten? The rite is already complete.
For the first time in a thousand years, the very rules he had prided himself on have turned their lance against him.
You stand a half-step behind her, your voice low, but your words resounding.
My job's done. A detective's duty is to uncover the truth.
What comes next belongs to the undertaker.
She closes her eyes. When they open again, her crystalline red gaze is perfectly clear.
The moment her power fully awakens, the entire forbidden grounds shudder.
The Mist that has churned for a thousand years has stilled.
Beyond the ring of light, the lurking wraiths sink low as one, bowing to their new master.
Through the cracks in the cobblestones, white flowers bloom in silence. One by one, they spread from beneath her feet all the way to the Lone Emperor.
No... this can't be... That power is mine! The forbidden grounds are mine!
Don't listen to her! I am Velossen! I am the one who—
His armies have already yielded to a new sovereign before he could.
Nirvatia walks forward, her scythe in hand, treading over the white flowers.
Ancient syllables spill from her lips—
This is the lament she sang to a little girl on a morning on Mistrellis Street.
Now, she sings it for a thousand years of lost souls.
"I will guide you through the clouds."
"I will guide you through the clouds."
The Lone Emperor convulses violently within the song, and one by one, his blurred faces turn toward her.
"To a place where you may rest."
"To a place where you may rest."
She comes to a halt before the Lone Emperor, gazing up at the countless faces layered upon one another.
Your sins... I have witnessed them all. Your suffering... I have witnessed that too.
Her blade rises, its tip aimed straight at the dark core lurking deep within the figure.
You who have sinned without consequence—
I will see you to your destined end.
A dark scythe unfurls in her grasp, its blade stretching out like a curtain of night falling into place.
Her blade cuts through a curse a thousand years in the making.
The Lone Emperor splits apart from the center.
The dark core at the deepest point of the shadow convulses and writhes in futile desperation amid the fading light, its dying shriek swallowed whole by the lingering echo of the song—
Layer after layer of human forms peel away and dissolve in the blade's light, like a weary traveler finally freed of burdens. It crumbles into motes of white dust, then into nothing.
The murmurs fade to a sigh.
A curse of a thousand years has ended at last.
